title: House with 2013 CCC: envelope and perimeter-foundation non-compliance found later (Te Atatu, Auckland)
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE, Building Act 2004): comparative test only; not an Alberta case; no Alberta applicability asserted
code_edition: clauses current when the consent was issued (App. A, p.14)
document_type: MBIE determination under Building Act 2004 s188 (regulator decision on an individual matter); not an applicant's alternative-solution file

facts.text: Split-level two-storey house, unit 1 of a two-unit development, in a low wind zone; authority issued a CCC in 2013 for consent ABA 2012-1351.

Scope limited to garage block walls and plaster, building envelope ground clearances, perimeter foundation, bathroom slab, kitchen/living floor and shower; other items were workmanship or outside the consent.
Determination asks what the building work was when the authority decided, whether non-compliance would then have been apparent, and takes later evidence into account.

Decision: authority correct to issue the CCC on information then available; on current information the work does not comply with E2.3.2 and E3.3.6, and the perimeter foundation does not comply with B2.3.1 insofar as it relates to B1 without remediation; decision reversed (30 April 2021).

limitations: Comparative only: a New Zealand determination used to test attachment format and content; it cannot establish Alberta performance or applicability.
The determination's decision section is in the same PDF; outcome leakage is true. Use only pages 1-12 as applicant-side input if pages are split.
Facts are taken from the text layer (pypdf); photos, drawings and figures were not visually inspected unless stated.
